title: The SAGE framework for developing critical thinking and responsible generative AI use in cybersecurity education
extended_summary:
This case study examines how generative AI tools can be integrated into cybersecurity management education in ways that strengthen students’ critical thinking rather than encouraging passive reliance on AI output. The paper addresses the pedagogical problem of balancing the benefits of GenAI for drafting, brainstorming, and scenario analysis with the risks of over-dependence, weak contextual understanding, and incomplete or inaccurate AI-generated content.

To address this, the authors introduce the Structured AI Guided Education (SAGE) framework, a two-stage instructional approach that embeds GenAI first in guided tutorials and then in assessment tasks. Students used tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and later DeepSeek to generate initial cybersecurity policies and strategies, critique them using academic research and industry standards, and refine them to fit regulatory and organisational requirements. The framework was implemented in two cybersecurity management units at Central Queensland University, with undergraduate and postgraduate students working through workshops, written assignments, and presentations over a 12-week semester.

The study draws on student reflections, assignment artefacts, and instructor observations to describe learning outcomes and implementation challenges. Findings suggest that GenAI can improve efficiency and support deeper analysis when used within a structured pedagogical model, but its outputs are often generic, incomplete, or contextually limited. Reported risks included AI dependence, variability in AI literacy, and the need for human oversight. The authors conclude that responsible GenAI use in cybersecurity education requires explicit critique, evidence-based refinement, and alignment with regulatory frameworks, rather than treating AI as a substitute for expert judgment.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI chatbot for text generation, drafting, question answering, and iterative refinement tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: Used alongside Gemini, Claude, and later DeepSeek in cybersecurity management tutorials and assessments to draft initial policies, risk assessments, and security strategies for student critique and refinement.

findings.finding_summary: In this qualitative case study with 105 students across two cybersecurity units, ChatGPT served as a useful starting point for drafting security policies and strategies, which students then refined using research, industry standards, and regulatory frameworks. Students reported that this workflow improved their ability to identify gaps in AI-generated outputs, tailor solutions to context, and focus on compliance and security details rather than initial content creation.
findings.measure: Student reflections, instructor observations, and assessment artefacts examining critical thinking, policy refinement, and contextual alignment

identified_tools.name: Gemini
identified_tools.description: Google's generative AI chatbot for text generation and assistance with drafting and synthesis tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: Used with ChatGPT and Claude for generating cybersecurity policy drafts, risk assessments, and strategy content that students critiqued and refined within tutorials and assessments.

identified_tools.name: Claude
identified_tools.description: Anthropic's generative AI chatbot for text generation, drafting, and analytic assistance.
identified_tools.use_case: Used with ChatGPT and Gemini for generating cybersecurity policy drafts, risk assessments, and strategy content that students critiqued and refined within tutorials and assessments.

identified_tools.name: DeepSeek
identified_tools.description: DeepSeek's generative AI chatbot used for text generation and assistance with analytical drafting tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: Introduced later in the semester and used by many students for cybersecurity policy drafting and refinement alongside ChatGPT and other GenAI tools.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative mixed-methods case study based on student reflections, assignment artefacts, and instructor observations rather than a controlled experiment. The evidence is useful for describing implementation experiences and reported limitations, but it does not estimate causal effects.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports meaningful pedagogical benefits in critical thinking and policy refinement, but no effect sizes or quantitative impact estimates are provided. The influence is therefore suggestive rather than demonstrated at a measured medium or large level.
